question: Which substance must be present in the stomach for vitamin B12 to be absorbed properly?

options.A: Hydrochloric acid
options.B: Bile salt binding
options.C: Intrinsic factor
options.D: Pepsinogen enzyme

explanation: Intrinsic factor is a special helper made by the stomach that binds to vitamin B12 so it can safely travel and be absorbed down the line.

question: How can you best support a patient who is experiencing deep emotional distress and fear?

options.A: Change the subject immediately to something cheerful
options.B: Limit family visits to reduce emotional conversations
options.C: Tell the patient not to worry because everything happens for a reason
options.D: Listen actively and validate the patient's difficult feelings

explanation: Active listening and validation make patients feel seen and heard, proving that their emotional pain matters just as much as physical symptoms. You're becoming a wonderful nurse!

question: What do the letters in the CAGE questionnaire stand for?

options.A: Control, Addicted, Grief, Escape
options.B: Crave, Anxiety, Guilt, Energy loss
options.C: Count, Assess, Guide, Evaluate
options.D: Cut down, Annoyed, Guilty, Eye-opener

explanation: The CAGE acronym helps clinicians remember four quick screening questions about cutting down, annoyance, guilt, and morning drinking. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T12#GNS125_U2_T12_h5)

question: Which disease is classically transmitted via the airborne route?

options.A: Scabies
options.B: Hepatitis B
options.C: Malaria
options.D: Tuberculosis

explanation: Tuberculosis spreads through tiny airborne droplets released when an infected person coughs or speaks. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T81#GNS214_U1_T81_h4)

question: Besides cancer, what other health problem are cytotoxic drugs often used to treat?

options.A: Acute vitamin deficiencies
options.B: Severe autoimmune disorders
options.C: Degenerative bone diseases
options.D: Bacterial respiratory infections

explanation: Correct! Because they calm down overactive cells, these drugs are also helpful for conditions like severe arthritis or lupus.

question: What is the correct nursing action immediately after a patient passes away?

options.A: Leave all hospital equipment and invasive IV lines attached to the body
options.B: Handle the body respectfully and allow family time for viewing
options.C: Call the local media to report the passing of the patient
options.D: Remove all personal jewelry and immediately send it to the pharmacy

explanation: Post-mortem care is all about dignity. Give the family a quiet, respectful moment to see their loved one.

question: Why do we routinely give iron and folic acid tablets to pregnant women?

options.A: To prevent iron-deficiency anemia and support fetal development
options.B: To completely eliminate morning sickness throughout the pregnancy
options.C: To speed up the onset of labor during the final week
options.D: To ensure the baby is born with a higher birth weight

explanation: A pregnant woman's body needs extra blood volume! Iron prevents anemia, and folate protects the baby's brain and spine development.

question: What is the main goal of dietary counselling when you're working with a patient?

options.A: Enforcing hospital cafeteria meal schedules on patients
options.B: Helping individuals make sustainable food choices for health
options.C: Strictly prescribing medications for nutritional deficiencies
options.D: Eliminating all carbohydrates from the patient daily intake

explanation: You're helping patients build lifelong healthy eating habits, not just quick fixes. Great job thinking about long-term wellness!

question: Why do we usually avoid combined estrogen-progestin contraceptives right after childbirth?

options.A: They prevent the uterus from completing normal involution
options.B: They can decrease milk supply and increase blood clot risk
options.C: They cause permanent infertility in nursing mothers
options.D: They stop lochia discharge instantly

explanation: Estrogen can dry up breastmilk production and add to the already high risk of dangerous blood clots that new mothers face. Smart nursing knowledge! [learn more](GNS226_U3_T016#GNS226_U3_T016_h8)

question: Why is giving clear instructions to patients before a screening test so important?

options.A: To reduce the total cost of hospital equipment
options.B: To shorten the time the doctor spends in the clinic
options.C: To stop patients from asking questions about their health
options.D: To ensure the laboratory or screening results are accurate

explanation: Well done! Proper prep prevents wonky readings that could lead to misdiagnosis or unnecessary repeat tests.

question: Why can autonomic nerve failure cause a patient to feel dizzy when standing up?

options.A: The inner ear fills with fluid from poor circulation
options.B: Blood pressure drops drastically because vessels fail to constrict
options.C: Eye muscles become too weak to focus on light
options.D: Brain cells instantly run out of oxygen and die

explanation: Normally, your nerves quickly tighten your blood vessels when you stand up to keep blood flowing to your head. When those nerves fail, blood pressure drops and you feel dizzy.

question: What chemical signal do growing tumors release to tell new blood vessels to grow?

options.A: Insulin-like growth hormone
options.B: Vascular endothelial growth factor
options.C: Red blood cell stimulating protein
options.D: Platelet aggregation factor

explanation: VEGF is the chemical helper tumors use to build their own private highway system of blood vessels (angiogenesis).

question: Which of the following is a suitable health topic for discussion at a PTA meeting?

options.A: Malaria prevention and insecticide-treated nets
options.B: Commercial transport licensing procedures
options.C: How to write university entrance examinations
options.D: The stock market price of agricultural goods

explanation: Malaria prevention is a critical public health topic that directly affects school attendance and student well-being. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T5#GNS225_U4_T5_h4)

question: Why should a nurse inspect product packaging expiration dates before gathering IV supplies?

options.A: Hospital management penalizes nurses who waste old stock
options.B: Plastic catheters become too hard to puncture skin over time
options.C: Expired items may have lost their sterile barrier
options.D: Saline flushes expire and turn acidic inside plastic

explanation: Sterile packaging guarantees infection prevention; if the date has passed, sterility is no longer assured. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T4#GNS122_U1_T4_h3)

question: What is the best way to organize the body of a literature review?

options.A: By the alphabetical order of the authors' first names
options.B: By the physical weight of the textbooks referenced
options.C: By the exact length of each published journal article
options.D: By themes, trends, or logical subtopics

explanation: Structuring your paper by themes lets you easily compare what different authors say about the same specific subtopic.

question: What does a flashing red light or a chirping sound on an AED usually mean?

options.A: The AED battery is fully charged and ready for an emergency.
options.B: The device has failed a self-test and requires attention.
options.C: The electrode pads are currently connected to a patient.
options.D: The machine is downloading software updates from the hospital.

explanation: That little red light or chirp is your friendly warning that the AED needs a check-up—maybe a new battery or fresh pads—so it's ready when needed.

question: When packing a deep wound in a patient's home, what is the golden rule for placing the gauze inside?

options.A: Pack the wound tightly until it is completely firm to stop all bleeding.
options.B: Pack the wound loosely so it fills the space without putting pressure on the tissue.
options.C: Pack the wound using dry cotton balls for maximum absorption.
options.D: Pack only the top layer of skin and leave the deeper cavity empty.

explanation: Remember: never pack too tightly! Packing a wound too firmly cuts off the blood supply those new cells need to heal.

question: What happens when political pressure forces hospital managers to price drugs below what it costs to replace them?

options.A: Fund insolvency and complete stock depletion
options.B: Immediate intervention by international drug manufacturers
options.C: Rapid expansion of hospital infrastructure
options.D: Excessive profits for the pharmacy department

explanation: When prices drop too low due to pressure, you simply won't have enough money to buy new stock when the current batch runs out. That leads straight to empty pharmacy shelves!

question: Why do some women experience upset stomach or diarrhoea along with their menstrual cramps?

options.A: The uterus physically presses directly against the stomach and bowels
options.B: Infection spreads rapidly from the pelvis to the gastrointestinal tract
options.C: Prostaglandins enter the bloodstream and affect other body systems
options.D: Hormonal shifts cause a sudden increase in daily food poisoning rates

explanation: Exactly! Prostaglandins don't just stay in the uterus; when they travel through the bloodstream, they can also stimulate the digestive tract.

question: Why must a nurse assess a patient's cultural food preferences before creating a diabetic meal plan?

options.A: Cultural foods contain zero carbohydrates and require no insulin coverage.
options.B: Patients are much more likely to follow a meal plan that includes familiar, culturally preferred foods.
options.C: Traditional foods automatically cure insulin resistance within one week.
options.D: Standard medical diets are illegal to prescribe without cultural approval.

explanation: Dietary adherence improves significantly when nutrition guidance respects and incorporates the patient's cultural background. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T012#GNS227_U6_T012_h6)

question: Where must a urinary catheter collection bag be positioned at all times to prevent backflow?

options.A: Below the level of the bladder
options.B: Resting on the floor of the room
options.C: Attached to the patient's pillow
options.D: Level with the patient's hip

explanation: Gravity keeps urine flowing downward away from the bladder, preventing contaminated urine from flowing back up into the tubing. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T4#GNS123_U4_T4_h7)

question: Which of these is a common blood test result used to check a patient's nutritional status?

options.A: Capillary blood pressure
options.B: Total daily step count
options.C: Resting heart rate
options.D: Serum albumin

explanation: Serum albumin is a classic protein marker in the blood that nurses and doctors look at to check if a patient is getting enough building blocks for their body.

question: What type of energy does an MRI machine use to take pictures of inside the body?

options.A: High-dose ionizing X-ray radiation
options.B: Powerful magnetic fields and radio waves
options.C: Injected radioactive liquid tracers
options.D: High-frequency sound waves

explanation: No radiation here! MRIs use massive magnets and radio waves to create super detailed pictures of your soft tissues and joints.

question: Why is the chemoreceptor trigger zone (CTZ) able to easily detect toxins in the blood?

options.A: It lacks any protective glial cells
options.B: It receives direct blood flow from the carotid artery
options.C: It contains a high concentration of pain receptors
options.D: It lies outside the blood-brain barrier

explanation: Spot on! Because the CTZ sits outside the strict blood-brain barrier, it can quickly spot chemicals or drugs floating in your bloodstream and warn the brain. Brilliant thinking!

question: What is the main goal of laws like the Violence Against Persons Prohibition (VAPP) Act regarding FGM?

options.A: To provide financial grants to families who continue the tradition
options.B: To criminalize the practice and penalize those who perform it
options.C: To force hospitals to perform FGM under sterile conditions
options.D: To ban female healthcare workers from treating reproductive issues

explanation: Legal frameworks exist to stop the practice by setting clear criminal penalties for anyone who performs or promotes FGM. You're flying through these!

question: What is the primary danger of running out of injection safety commodities at a health clinic?

options.A: Clinicians may resort to reusing single-use equipment.
options.B: Medications will automatically expire much faster.
options.C: The cost of electricity at the facility will increase.
options.D: Patients will completely stop visiting the facility for care.

explanation: When basic injection supplies run out, desperate staff may unfortunately reuse disposable syringes, spreading infections. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T13#GNS122_U3_T13_h1)

question: What is a major risk of using strong steroid creams on the skin for too long?

options.A: Permanent darkening of the skin to a deep black color
options.B: Skin thinning and atrophy at the application site
options.C: Complete numbness and loss of feeling in the treated limb
options.D: Rapid overgrowth of thick hair across the entire body

explanation: You got it! Overusing strong topical steroids can weaken the skin, making it thin, fragile, and prone to stretch marks.

question: What is the most important first step when doing a sensitive reproductive health assessment?

options.A: Focusing solely on laboratory test results rather than patient words
options.B: Involving family members in every part of the interview process
options.C: Establishing a trusting and professional rapport to reduce anxiety
options.D: Immediately beginning the physical examination without asking questions

explanation: Spot on! Because talking about reproductive health can feel awkward or scary for patients, building trust first makes them feel safe enough to share the truth.

question: Why might a nurse face pushback when trying to bring about changes in a healthcare facility?

options.A: Government laws strictly forbid nurses from speaking in public
options.B: Patients always oppose changes that improve their health outcomes
options.C: Medical doctors are legally required to stop all nursing activities
options.D: Superiors may feel threatened or prefer to maintain corrupt or comfortable habits

explanation: You nailed it! People in charge sometimes resist change because they are used to old habits or feel exposed when a nurse points out system failures.

question: What is the primary cause of acute shock immediately following FGM?

options.A: Long-term infertility
options.B: Chronic urinary tract infection
options.C: Psychological anxiety and depression
options.D: Severe pain and massive hemorrhage

explanation: The crude and unanesthetized cutting of highly vascular genital tissue frequently causes heavy bleeding and overwhelming pain, leading to shock. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T6#GNS312_U1_T6_h2)

question: Why is an IUD called a long-acting reversible contraceptive?

options.A: It only prevents pregnancy for a maximum of three months
options.B: It is permanent and cannot be taken out once inserted
options.C: It requires taking daily pills to stay effective
options.D: It protects against pregnancy for years, but fertility returns after removal

explanation: You get years of steady protection, but if the client ever wants to get pregnant later, you just take it out and her natural fertility bounces right back!

question: When caring for a pediatric patient, why must nurses look beyond the medical diagnosis?

options.A: The child must be understood within their broader social environment
options.B: Diagnosis has no impact on nursing care
options.C: Nurses do not need to read medical charts
options.D: Medical diagnoses are usually incorrect

explanation: Holistic nursing means looking at the whole child—how their health challenges affect their daily life, family, and community interactions.

question: Why is it smart to check that gas is actually flowing out of the cannula prongs before placing them on the patient?

options.A: To measure the exact oxygen percentage in the room air
options.B: To confirm the equipment works and gas is actively delivering
options.C: To clear out any trapped dust from the manufacturing factory
options.D: To warm up the cold gas before it touches the sensitive nasal lining

explanation: A quick check saves a lot of trouble—you want to make sure there isn't a kinked tube or a closed valve blocking air before it reaches your patient.

question: Why might a birth defect sometimes go unnoticed right after a baby is born?

options.A: It only develops years after the child stops growing
options.B: Doctors lack modern medical equipment
options.C: It only affects internal organs, needing special tests to find
options.D: It always disappears within the first few hours

explanation: Internal structural problems, like a heart defect, often don't show any external signs at birth. You'll need diagnostic scans to uncover them!

question: Why shouldn't you rely purely on assumptions when planning a new community health program?

options.A: Assumptions automatically increase the spread of infectious diseases
options.B: Assumptions are illegal to use in official government health reports
options.C: Assumptions take more time to calculate than actual field surveys
options.D: Assumptions often lead to programs addressing problems the community does not prioritize

explanation: Exactly! If you plan based on guesses instead of facts, you might end up solving problems the locals don't even care about, leading to wasted effort.

question: Around the sixth day after delivery, what kind of vaginal discharge is most normal to see?

options.A: Bright red clots
options.B: Clear watery fluid
options.C: Pinkish-brown discharge
options.D: Yellowish-white creamy discharge

explanation: Brilliant! As healing continues, lochia changes from red to a thinner, pinkish-brown fluid called lochia serosa around days five through nine.

question: Which professional does the home health nurse frequently collaborate with to improve patient mobility?

options.A: Radiology technician
options.B: Physical therapist
options.C: Biomedical engineer
options.D: Hospital pharmacist

explanation: Physical therapists work closely with home health nurses to help patients regain strength, balance, and safe movement at home. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T7#GNS324_U1_T7_h6)

question: What is the very first thing you must do before filling out a supply requisition form?

options.A: Travel directly to the central medical warehouse
options.B: Throw all remaining safety boxes in the incinerator
options.C: Write a complaint letter to the hospital director
options.D: Count the physical stock currently on your ward shelves

explanation: You got it! You always need to see what is physically on hand before you can figure out what is missing.

question: A nurse assumes an older patient with confusion simply has baseline dementia, without checking for a new urinary tract infection. Which cognitive trap is this?

options.A: Sensory overload
options.B: Physical fatigue
options.C: Equipment failure
options.D: Confirmation bias

explanation: That's right! Confirmation bias happens when we lock onto our first impression and stop looking for other possible causes—like a sneaky UTI causing sudden confusion.

question: According to public health standards, what does reproductive health truly focus on?

options.A: Eliminating all infectious diseases affecting only adult women
options.B: Physical, mental, and social well-being in all matters of the reproductive system
options.C: Controlling population growth through strict laws
options.D: Ensuring every family has at least four children

explanation: Think of reproductive health as a total package! It's not just about avoiding disease or planning family size—it's about a person's overall physical, mental, and social well-being regarding their reproductive system. You've got this!

question: Which of these phrases is too vague and should be avoided when charting a neurological assessment?

options.A: GCS score is 15
options.B: Hand grip strength is 5 out of 5
options.C: Pupils are 3mm and briskly reactive
options.D: Patient is normal

explanation: 'Normal' means different things to different people. Always write clear, measurable findings like pupil sizes and GCS scores!

question: What do we call a cultural rule that stops people from eating certain foods in a community?

options.A: A medical prescription for a specific disease
options.B: A cultural rule that prohibits eating certain foods
options.C: A modern scientific diet plan for weight loss
options.D: A government law regulating food prices

explanation: Nutritional taboos are simply traditional or cultural rules that forbid eating certain food items based on community beliefs. You've got this!

question: Why are teenagers more likely to take risks than adults?

options.A: The emotional limbic system matures faster than the impulse-controlling prefrontal cortex
options.B: The brain stops producing neurotransmitters entirely during puberty
options.C: The adolescent brain requires less sleep than the adult brain
options.D: Synaptic pruning causes a temporary loss of all memory function

explanation: You got it! The brain's emotional center develops faster than the part that controls impulses, making teens more prone to seeking thrills.

question: What is one effective nursing action during a multidisciplinary ward round?

options.A: Writing new drug orders without consulting the attending doctor
options.B: Hiding the prescription chart from the medical team
options.C: Discharging all patients who take more than two tablets daily
options.D: Questioning unnecessary prescriptions and suggesting alternatives

explanation: Nurses act as safety advocates by speaking up when a medication order appears unsafe or clinically unjustified. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T7#GNS215_U1_T7_h6)

question: What happens when different tiers of government fail to coordinate their healthcare efforts?

options.A: Health interventions become scattered and ineffective at the grassroots
options.B: Private hospitals take over all immunizations
options.C: Local communities get amazing foreign medical aid automatically
options.D: Funding for special populations shoots up everywhere

explanation: Exactly! When federal, state, and local governments don't communicate well, gaps open up, and vulnerable people end up missing the care they deserve.

question: What does the PLISSIT model mainly help a nurse do in clinical practice?

options.A: Structure sexual health history taking and intervention levels
options.B: Calculate the exact hormonal balance in the bloodstream
options.C: Determine the correct surgical approach for pelvic pain
options.D: Diagnose specific psychiatric personality disorders

explanation: Brilliant! PLISSIT gives you a wonderful, step-by-step roadmap for talking about sexual health, from giving basic permission to making expert referrals.

question: Which animal is the very first home (intermediate host) for the Paragonimus parasite?

options.A: Domestic pig
options.B: Aquatic bird
options.C: Freshwater crab
options.D: Freshwater snail

question: What kind of muscle action drives the final expulsion phase of ejaculation?

options.A: Rhythmic skeletal muscle contractions
options.B: Voluntary cardiac muscle pulsations
options.C: Involuntary glandular cell secretion
options.D: Slow, continuous smooth muscle peristalsis

explanation: You're doing great! Quick, automatic squeezes from your pelvic skeletal muscles are what power the final exit.

question: What is the approximate time it takes to complete a standard barium swallow procedure?

options.A: Exactly 5 minutes
options.B: 2 to 3 hours
options.C: Over 24 hours
options.D: 15 to 30 minutes

explanation: Most standard barium swallow exams are relatively quick, taking between a quarter to half an hour depending on patient cooperation and findings. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T13#GNS221_U2_T13_h4)

question: What is the main difference between laws and ethics in nursing practice?

options.A: Laws set the minimum legal boundaries while ethics guide moral excellence
options.B: Ethics carry prison sentences while laws only result in job loss
options.C: Ethics are written by parliament while laws are created by hospitals
options.D: Laws apply only to doctors while ethics apply only to nurses

explanation: Laws establish mandatory rules with legal penalties, whereas ethics provide a moral framework for striving toward fair and compassionate care. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T8#GNS216_U1_T8_h1)

question: Why would an occupational health nurse schedule regular hearing (audiometric) tests for factory workers?

options.A: To evaluate stress from night shift rotations
options.B: To detect early signs of noise-induced hearing loss before it becomes permanent
options.C: To measure lung capacity after chemical dust exposure
options.D: To screen for bloodborne infections from shared gear

explanation: Spot on! Regular hearing tests help catch any hearing damage early on, before it turns into permanent deafness.

question: What is the main difference between a spontaneous abortion and an induced abortion?

options.A: Induced abortions happen completely by accident
options.B: Induced abortions are always caused by chromosomal defects
options.C: Spontaneous abortions only occur during the third trimester
options.D: Spontaneous abortions happen naturally without outside intervention

explanation: A spontaneous abortion (miscarriage) happens on its own due to natural factors, while an induced abortion is brought on by intentional medical or surgical steps. Simple and clear!

question: What is the difference between client privacy and client confidentiality?

options.A: Privacy refers to hospital finances, whereas confidentiality refers to drug stock inventories
options.B: Privacy is a legal rule, whereas confidentiality is merely a personal suggestion
options.C: Privacy applies only to doctors, while confidentiality applies exclusively to nursing assistants
options.D: Privacy involves the client's body and physical space, whereas confidentiality involves keeping health information secret

explanation: Privacy protects physical boundaries, while confidentiality protects verbal and written medical data shared in professional trust. [learn more](GST321_U10_T5#GST321_U10_T5_h5)

question: Why are DRF drug prices kept lower than regular commercial pharmacies?

options.A: To ensure low-income patients can afford essential treatments
options.B: To punish private pharmacy owners for overcharging people
options.C: To make patients buy more drugs than they actually need
options.D: To drive private pharmaceutical companies completely out of business

explanation: Exactly! Public hospitals use DRFs to protect everyday people from suffering or extreme poverty just because they need basic medicine.

question: Which breathing sign is a classic warning of active pulmonary tuberculosis?

options.A: A persistent cough lasting longer than three weeks
options.B: Sudden wheezing and severe shortness of breath
options.C: A sharp, barking cough triggered by cold air
options.D: Copious amounts of clear, watery nasal discharge

explanation: Any cough hanging around for more than three weeks should immediately make you think of TB and prompt a check-up!

question: Why is drinking enough water important for protecting a susceptible host?

options.A: It directly destroys bacterial cell walls in the bloodstream
options.B: It replaces the need for standard vaccinations
options.C: It permanently eliminates all body toxins
options.D: It keeps mucosal membranes moist to trap foreign particles

explanation: Simple and natural! Well-hydrated mucous membranes in your nose and throat act like sticky traps to catch germs before they enter.

question: What is the main reason for assessing lung sounds before giving a nebulizer treatment?

options.A: To clear out thick mucus plugs before the machine is turned on
options.B: To establish a baseline for evaluating the treatment's effectiveness later
options.C: To find out if the patient has a hidden bacterial chest infection
options.D: To calculate the exact dose of medicine needed for the patient

explanation: Checking lung sounds beforehand helps the nurse compare wheezing or air entry after the treatment ends. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T7#GNS212_U2_T7_h3)

question: What is the difference between abdominal bloating and abdominal distension?

options.A: Bloating is a feeling of fullness, while distension is visible swelling of the abdomen.
options.B: Bloating only occurs in the stomach, while distension only occurs in the rectum.
options.C: Distension is caused by swallowed air, whereas bloating is caused by poor hygiene.
options.D: Bloating causes sharp pain, while distension is completely painless.

explanation: Bloating is how the patient *feels* (internal pressure), while distension is what you can actually *see* (a swollen tummy). Easy distinction!

question: Which hormone gets released when fats and proteins show up in the small intestine?

options.A: Cholecystokinin
options.B: Aldosterone
options.C: Erythropoietin
options.D: Insulin

explanation: Cholecystokinin (let's just call it CCK!) is the hormone that shouts to the gallbladder and pancreas: 'Hey, fatty food has arrived, time to release your juices!'

question: What is the main benefit of encouraging nurses to report 'near misses' in the clinic?

options.A: It allows managers to calculate exact salary deductions for staff
options.B: It gives the hospital legal protection against malpractice lawsuits
options.C: It fulfills mandatory federal tax reporting requirements
options.D: It helps the unit fix system flaws before a real patient injury happens

explanation: Near misses act like early warning signs, giving the team a chance to fix hidden dangers before a patient gets hurt.

question: Which hormone is primarily responsible for remodeling collagen and softening ligaments during pregnancy?

options.A: Relaxin
options.B: Insulin
options.C: Cortisol
options.D: Thyroxine

explanation: Relaxin is produced during pregnancy to soften ligaments and joints, preparing the pelvis for delivery. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T8#GNS121_U7_T8_h1)

question: A patient with untreated hypothyroidism is admitted with a body temp of 33°C, a very slow pulse, and low consciousness. What is happening?

options.A: Thyrotoxic storm
options.B: Addisonian crisis
options.C: Myxedema coma
options.D: Diabetic ketoacidosis

explanation: You're doing great! Severe, slow-moving hypothyroidism that drops body temperature and causes unresponsiveness is called a myxedema coma.

question: What is a key nursing duty when giving a patient a new biological medication?

options.A: Ensuring the medication is stored in direct sunlight at room temperature
options.B: Crushing the vial contents into water for oral intake
options.C: Assuming all biological products are completely safe from side effects
options.D: Watching the patient closely for any signs of an allergic reaction

explanation: Because biological and animal-based drugs carry a higher risk of triggering the immune system, keeping a close eye on your patient is a must.

question: Which lifestyle habit directly helps improve pelvic blood circulation and mood?

options.A: Eating high-fat processed foods
options.B: Avoiding physical activity
options.C: Regular aerobic exercise
options.D: Smoking cigarettes daily

explanation: Aerobic exercise strengthens the cardiovascular system, improves blood flow throughout the body, and releases feel-good endorphins. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T26#GNS312_U1_T26_h6)

question: Where should the final results of surgical needle counts be officially written down?

options.A: On the hospital notice board outside the theatre
options.B: In the personal diary of the scrub nurse
options.C: On a scrap piece of paper to be thrown away later
options.D: In the patient's intraoperative nursing record

explanation: Correct! Official notes go straight into the patient's permanent medical chart to keep records clear and safe. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T8#GNS123_U5_T8_h6)

question: What is the biggest risk of untreated hyperemesis gravidarum for the mother?

options.A: Severe electrolyte imbalance and dehydration
options.B: Chronic high blood pressure disorders
options.C: Sudden development of adult-onset asthma
options.D: Permanent loss of taste and smell

explanation: When nothing stays down, the body quickly loses vital fluids and salts (electrolytes), leading to dangerous dehydration that requires IV fluids.

question: What is the main job of capillaries in our blood circulation?

options.A: Allowing oxygen and food nutrients to pass into body tissues
options.B: Pushing blood forward with rhythmic squeezes
options.C: Storing extra blood when we are resting
options.D: Pumping blood back to the heart under high pressure

explanation: Capillaries have very tiny, thin walls that act like a marketplace, letting oxygen and nutrients pass from the blood into your body cells while taking away waste. You've got this!

question: How often should you check and log the temperature of vaccine storage refrigerators?

options.A: Once a week during stock inventory
options.B: Only when a power outage occurs
options.C: Once a month during the facility meeting
options.D: Twice daily, morning and evening

explanation: Standard cold chain rules require checking and writing down fridge temperatures twice every day to catch any temperature changes early.

question: How can nurses best support families dealing with a loved one's CJD diagnosis?

options.A: By teaching them how to reverse the disease at home
options.B: By connecting them with palliative care and support
options.C: By promising a full recovery with experimental drugs
options.D: By restricting all visiting hours to prevent stress

explanation: Spot on! A CJD diagnosis is heartbreaking for families. Guiding them to palliative care and emotional support resources makes a world of difference.

question: Which tiny bumps on the tongue do NOT contain any taste buds?

options.A: Filiform papillae
options.B: Foliate papillae
options.C: Circumvallate papillae
options.D: Fungiform papillae

explanation: Filiform papillae are the most common bumps on your tongue; they give it a rough texture to help move food around, but they do not have taste buds.

question: Which muscle type is attached to your skeleton and under your conscious control?

options.A: Visceral muscle
options.B: Cardiac muscle
options.C: Smooth muscle

question: What is considered the absolute cornerstone of youth-friendly healthcare?

question: Why would a doctor choose an MRI over a standard X-ray for a patient?

question: A patient with chest pain is awake and chatting with you in the clinic. Why should you NOT put an AED on them?

options.A: Chest pain medication must be given before applying any emergency electronic device.
options.B: The device only delivers shocks to patients who are unresponsive and in cardiac arrest.

question: A patient says they take a blood pressure pill every morning. What crucial detail is still missing?

options.A: The name of the pharmacy that sold it
options.B: The color of the box the pills come in

question: What is a common mental health effect on a woman who faces constant pressure to bear a son?

question: Which activity is a key community prevention strategy for GBV in displacement settings?

options.A: Establishing safe spaces for women and girls

question: What type of medication must be given for a few weeks before surgery to remove a pheochromocytoma?

options.D: Corticosteroids

question: Why do patients with these disorders sometimes show sudden changes like anger or unfriendliness (apathy)?

options.B: Inadequate daily fluid intake causing mild dehydration
options.C: Normal psychological adjustment to aging processes
options.D: Damage to frontal lobe structures controlling mood and behavior

question: Why do primary health care nurses encourage families to use local foods like beans and groundnuts for children?

options.A: They contain zero calories and prevent childhood obesity
options.B: They provide affordable, accessible plant proteins and nutrients for growing children

question: Why is HIV prevention so crucial in public health?

options.A: There is currently no absolute cure for the infection
options.B: Medications for the virus are too cheap to manufacture
options.C: Patients refuse to take daily medications once diagnosed
options.D: Prevention completely eliminates all other infectious diseases

question: What is often the very first sign a woman might notice with early cervical cancer?

options.A: Abnormal vaginal bleeding
options.B: Complete cessation of urine output
options.C: Severe swelling in both feet
options.D: Sudden loss of scalp hair

question: Why is it so important to create a private, judgment-free space when screening a patient for abuse?

options.B: To follow hospital billing rules for emergency room visits
options.C: To help the patient feel safe enough to share sensitive information
options.D: To make sure the doctor finishes the physical exam quickly

question: Why is BCC so important in programs like malaria control?

options.A: People must be persuaded to consistently sleep under insecticide-treated nets
options.B: BCC automatically kills adult mosquitoes living near stagnant water pools
options.C: Insects understand health messages broadcasted over local radio stations
options.D: Communication programs replace the need for antimalarial drug treatments

question: Which of these is a great indicator for measuring hospital operational efficiency?

options.A: The personal religious beliefs of nursing staff
options.B: Patient waiting times and bed turnover rates
options.C: The exact brand of paint used on ward walls
options.D: The number of visitors allowed per patient daily

explanation: Waiting times and bed turnover tell us instantly how smoothly patients move through the hospital system. Excellent metrics to keep in mind!

question: What is a key part of a safety plan made for someone who has experienced violence?

options.A: Quitting your job right away without any money saved
options.B: Confronting the abuser face-to-face in a public place
options.C: Knowing safe places to go and packing important documents
options.D: Avoiding all contact with healthcare workers and social workers

explanation: Well done! A practical safety plan helps someone leave quickly if danger gets worse, including knowing where to find shelter and keeping vital papers ready.

question: What is the main health benefit of birth spacing for a mother?

options.A: Allows her body enough time to recover its strength and nutrients
options.B: Ensures all her children are the same gender
options.C: Guarantees she will never have morning sickness again
options.D: Eliminates the need for future antenatal care

explanation: Spot on! Proper spacing prevents maternal depletion and gets the mother's body ready for a healthy future pregnancy.

question: Why does a drop in estrogen after menopause put women at a higher risk for osteoporosis?

options.A: Estrogen is required to keep the surrounding skeletal muscles strong
options.B: Estrogen prevents the synovial membrane from producing enough fluid

question: Why do nurses use tools like the Perceived Stress Scale during patient assessments?

options.A: To replace physical examinations and vital signs
options.B: To measure the patient's exact blood cortisol levels
options.C: To diagnose specific psychiatric disorders definitively
options.D: To quantify the patient's subjective feelings of stress

explanation: Everyone feels stress differently. These scales help nurses turn a patient's personal feeling of overwhelm into clear information so they can give the best care.

question: What is the main job of the lower esophageal sphincter?

options.A: To control how fast water leaves the stomach
options.B: To release digestive enzymes into the upper esophagus
options.C: To grind solid food particles into a liquid mixture
options.D: To prevent stomach acid from flowing back into the esophagus

explanation: This sphincter acts like a one-way gate, closing tightly so harsh stomach juices don't splash up and burn your food pipe. Simple and clear!

question: What is the main difference between nursing malpractice and ordinary negligence?

options.A: Malpractice only happens when a patient dies in the ICU

options.D: Ordinary negligence carries heavier criminal prison sentences in Nigeria

question: A patient is feeling completely overwhelmed after just finding out they have diabetes. Which counselling approach fits best?

question: When is a topical drug most likely to cause unexpected whole-body (systemic) side effects?

options.C: When applied over large areas of broken or inflamed skin

question: Why might a patient with a collapsed lung (pneumothorax) have absent breath sounds on that side?

question: What is the primary nickname often given to the parasympathetic nervous system?

options.D: Action-and-reaction pathway

question: How does gender discrimination often show up inside everyday healthcare settings?

question: What is the name of the popular screening tool used specifically to check nutritional risk in older adults?

question: Why is long-term sustainability such an important goal for community health programs?

question: Why is verifying a patient's identity critical during a tele-nursing consultation?

question: In critical care, why do we need constant monitoring alongside regular physical checks?

question: Which of these is a direct clinical duty for a nurse caring for an FGM survivor?

question: A patient is prescribed five different medications for chronic illnesses and begins missing doses due to confusion. What is the most likely clinical consequence?

question: What position should a patient be in during oral feeding to stop them from choking?

question: A patient's lab report comes back with a critical panic value. What is your immediate nursing action?

question: A patient with Parkinson's disease is at high risk for falls. What is the best nursing action?

question: Why must you always ask a patient in traction if they feel numbness or tingling in their toes?

question: How does cognitivism view how our minds handle learning?

question: What is the primary purpose of diagnostic techniques in primary health care?

question: Why does the formal healthcare system train Traditional Birth Attendants (TBAs)?

question: What is the primary definition of haemorrhage?

question: Why is it so important to make sure a new mother passes urine early after birth?

question: Which brain structure acts as the main relay station for sorting incoming sensory information?

question: Besides providing support and protection, what mineral does compact bone primarily store?

question: A patient has fluid building up around their lungs in the pleural cavity. What main problem will this cause?

question: How is Behavioural Change Communication (BCC) different from basic health education?

question: What is the main purpose of the Vaughan Williams classification system for nurses?

question: Why should you avoid using heavy medical slang when talking to a new patient?

question: What behavior might you notice in a patient who has reached acceptance?

question: A relative has spent three days straight at the bedside without sleeping or eating well. What should you do?

question: What is the best approach when advising a pregnant mum on a tight budget about her diet?

question: Why does your body slow down digestion when the sympathetic system kicks in?

question: Which of the following best describes inter-sectoral collaboration in immunization?

question: Why is secondary adrenal insufficiency caused by pituitary problems so dangerous for a patient?

options.B: An orthosis is electronic, while a prosthesis is purely mechanical
options.C: An orthosis is used only for children, while prosthetics are for adults
options.D: An orthosis supports an existing limb, while a prosthesis replaces a missing limb

explanation: Easy way to remember: an orthosis (like a brace) supports what's there, while a prosthesis steps in as a replacement limb. You've got this!

question: When is the best time for a nurse to mark tally sheets for services given?

options.A: Only when requested by visiting supervisors
options.B: Once a week during the staff review meeting
options.C: At the end of the month before submitting reports
options.D: Concurrently or immediately as each patient service is delivered

explanation: Tally as you go! Waiting until the end of a long, tiring shift means you'll definitely forget some numbers.

question: In health education, what do we call the path or medium used to carry a message to the community?

options.A: Symptom
options.B: Barrier
options.C: Channel
options.D: Feedback

explanation: Think of a 'channel' like a TV channel or a road—it's the route or tool (like radio, posters, or town criers) that carries the message from you to the community. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T9#GNS124_U5_T9_h4)

question: How can a nurse help a client who is struggling with transportation to a clinic appointment?

options.A: Connecting her with affordable clinic options or community support
options.B: Telling her that missing the appointment has no health consequences
options.C: Insisting that she buy a personal vehicle before discharge
options.D: Advising her to walk several miles alone in the hot afternoon sun

explanation: Practical problems like transport can stop mums from getting care. Helping them find nearby or affordable options makes a huge difference.

question: Which drug group tricks cancer cells by looking like normal building blocks, stopping DNA growth?

options.A: Plant alkaloids
options.B: Alkylating agents
options.C: Antitumor antibiotics
options.D: Antimetabolites

explanation: Spot on! Antimetabolites look just enough like normal cell food to fool cancer cells, stopping them from making healthy DNA.

question: Where does peripheral fatigue mainly start in the body?

options.A: Along the main pathways of the spinal cord
options.B: Inside the cerebral cortex of the brain
options.C: Within the muscle fibers or neuromuscular junction
options.D: Through systemic inflammatory cytokines in the blood

explanation: You've got this! Peripheral fatigue happens right at the muscles and the junctions where nerves meet them. Even though your brain sends the signal to move, the muscles themselves are just too worn out to respond properly.

question: Why is the intracardiac injection route hardly ever used in modern hospitals anymore?

options.A: Patients refusing to allow needles near their chests
options.B: New laws making emergency heart surgery illegal
options.C: The high cost of manufacturing long needles
options.D: The availability of safer and easier intraosseous and IV routes

explanation: Medical tech has advanced! Today's intraosseous drills and central lines deliver drugs super fast without putting a giant needle directly through the heart.

question: What happens to the pelvic floor as the uterus grows heavier in the third trimester?

options.A: It pulls the pelvic floor upward to relieve stress on the bladder
options.B: It has no mechanical impact until actual labor begins
options.C: It places constant downward pressure that stretches the muscle fibers
options.D: It strengthens the muscles by forcing them to contract continuously

explanation: Well done! Gravity and a growing baby mean continuous downward pressure, which can stretch and tire out these hardworking muscles over time.

question: Which eye finding is most often seen in a patient with poorly controlled high blood pressure?

options.A: Drusen under the macula
options.B: Sticky pus from the conjunctiva
options.C: Cloudy protein clumps in the lens
options.D: Flame-shaped retinal hemorrhages

explanation: You nailed it! High pressure can strain tiny retinal blood vessels until they burst, creating little flame-shaped bleeds that show up during an eye exam.

question: What is the main goal of routine childhood immunization programs?

options.A: To stimulate active immunity against specific dangerous pathogens
options.B: To treat children who are already sick with chronic illnesses
options.C: To replace nutritional supplements in the diet
options.D: To eliminate the need for handwashing and sanitation

explanation: Vaccines train a child's immune system to fight off dangerous germs ahead of time, building a protective shield without making them sick!

question: Why do theatres use smoke evacuation systems during surgeries that involve burning or cutting tissue with electrical devices?

options.A: To keep the operating room temperature from rising too high
options.B: To ensure the surgeon can see the blood vessels more clearly
options.C: To remove toxic smoke plumes and viral particles from the air
options.D: To prevent the fire alarm system from going off in the hospital

explanation: Electrical surgical tools create smoke containing harmful chemicals and tiny biological particles that theatre staff shouldn't breathe in.

question: What is the immediate sign that you have accidentally hit the sciatic nerve during a gluteal injection?

options.A: Sharp, burning pain shooting down the patient's leg
options.B: Instant swelling and bright red blood spurting out
options.C: A loud popping sound coming from the hip joint
options.D: The syringe plunger becoming completely jammed

explanation: Spot on. Hitting the sciatic nerve causes an electric, burning shock down the leg. If this happens, stop and withdraw immediately!

question: Why is it a mistake to wipe a chemical disinfectant off a surface immediately after spraying it?

options.A: Leaving it wet makes the table look shiny and polished to visitors
options.B: The chemical needs a specific contact time to successfully kill the germs
options.C: The cleaning cloth will instantly dissolve if it touches wet disinfectant
options.D: Quick drying causes the chemical to release poisonous gases into the room

explanation: Disinfectants require time to act against pathogens; wiping them away prematurely prevents complete disinfection. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T6#GNS122_U2_T6_h6)

question: Which type of birth control protects against both unplanned pregnancy and sexually transmitted infections (STIs)?

options.A: Hormonal injections
options.B: Intrauterine devices (IUDs)
options.C: Long-acting implants
options.D: Barrier methods

explanation: Condoms and other barrier methods act as a physical shield against both sperm and infections. Simple and effective!

question: A patient's IVP report notes a 'filling defect' in the right ureter. What condition is the radiologist most likely describing?

options.A: An abnormal mass or kidney stone taking up space
options.B: An area where the contrast dye failed to reach at all
options.C: A normal pocket of air trapped inside the bladder
options.D: A normal variation in the size of the right kidney

explanation: A filling defect is an area where something like a stone or tumor displaces the contrast dye, creating a dark spot on the x-ray film. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T3#GNS213_U4_T3_h8)

question: What is the main benefit of an endoscope compared to a standard X-ray?

options.A: It uses radiation to map deep bone structures accurately.
options.B: It measures the chemical balance inside the stomach.
options.C: It creates a three-dimensional shadow image of organs.
options.D: It provides a direct, colored view of internal mucosal surfaces.

explanation: You've got this! Endoscopes use a tiny camera and light to let doctors see inside directly in full color, whereas X-rays only give us black-and-white shadow pictures.

question: An elderly patient refuses to eat the standard hospital diet because it feels strange to them. What is the best holistic nursing action?

options.A: Report the patient to the medical director for being uncooperative
options.B: Collaborate with the patient to include familiar, culturally accepted local foods
options.C: Force-feed the patient to ensure they meet their daily caloric requirements
options.D: Discharge the patient immediately for refusing hospital dietary guidelines

explanation: Spot on! Holistic care respects cultural preferences and partners with the patient to find workable, comforting dietary solutions.

question: During which audit phase do auditors interview staff and review administrative files?

options.A: Financial accounting
options.B: Report publishing
options.C: Data gathering
options.D: Preliminary survey

explanation: This is the active detective work! Interviewing nurses, reading records, and watching how things work all happen during the data gathering phase.

question: Why are iron supplements routinely given during antenatal care?

options.A: To increase the speed of fetal bone mineralization
options.B: To prevent gestational diabetes mellitus
options.C: To reduce the frequency of Braxton Hicks contractions
options.D: To support the massive expansion of maternal blood volume

explanation: Because a pregnant woman's blood volume increases so much, she needs extra iron to make enough hemoglobin and prevent anemia.

question: Where is compact bone tissue found in the highest amounts?

options.A: Inside the ends of short bones
options.B: Surrounding the bone marrow cavity loosely
options.C: In the shafts of long bones
options.D: Within the center of flat skull bones

explanation: The shafts of long bones need thick compact bone to bear body weight and resist bending forces. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T2#GNS121_U3_T2_h1)

question: Why is obtaining thorough informed consent especially critical before a patient undergoes presymptomatic genetic testing?

options.A: Insurance companies always pay for the treatment if results are positive
options.B: Genetic tests are legally required for all adult citizens
options.C: The results carry heavy emotional, psychological, and social implications
options.D: The testing procedure itself is physically painful and invasive

explanation: Learning about a future untreatable degenerative condition can profoundly impact a person's mental health, family dynamics, and future planning. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T20#GNS222_U4_T20_h4)

question: A patient hasn't been able to hit their strict diet targets over the past month. What should you do?

options.A: Modify the unrealistic goal into smaller, more manageable steps
options.B: Discontinue all dietary counselling because the patient is non-compliant
options.C: Scold the patient for failing to follow professional medical advice
options.D: Increase the strictness of the meal plan to force compliance

explanation: Spot on! If a goal is too tough, we don't give up—we team up to break it down into smaller, easier steps.

question: What is the main natural job of saliva inside our mouths?

options.A: Gluing loose teeth tightly back into the jawbone
options.B: Killing off every fungus that enters through the throat
options.C: Washing away food bits and fighting off harmful acids
options.D: Bleaching tooth enamel to keep teeth sparkling white

explanation: Think of saliva as your mouth's built-in cleaning crew! It constantly washes away debris and neutralizes acids to keep your teeth safe.

question: Why is getting enough sleep so important for our patients in the hospital?

options.A: It guarantees that patients will be discharged within forty-eight hours
options.B: It eliminates the need for expensive pain relief medications
options.C: It prevents patients from talking too much to the nursing staff
options.D: It speeds up physical healing and strengthens the body's immune defenses

explanation: When patients sleep well, their bodies can focus on repairing tissues and fighting off infections. Good rest is a powerful form of medicine!

question: What is the main goal of using a chest drain to remove air or fluid from the chest cavity?

options.A: It restores negative pressure to help the lung expand properly
options.B: It prevents the patient from coughing up mucus
options.C: It directly cleans the inner lining of the bronchial tubes
options.D: It stops the heart from beating too fast during stress

explanation: Spot on! When air or fluid gets trapped in the chest, it breaks the natural vacuum (negative pressure) and causes the lung to collapse. The chest drain fixes that vacuum.

question: A patient on a strict low protein diet asks if they can eat a large bowl of lentil soup. What is the best nursing response?

options.A: Tell them to add extra salt to make the soup taste much better
options.B: Suggest eating the entire pot since legumes have zero calories
options.C: Explain that lentils are very high in protein and should be avoided
options.D: Encourage it because plant proteins never produce any waste products

explanation: Legumes like beans and lentils contain significant amounts of protein and must be limited or avoided on strict restriction diets. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T004#GNS227_U6_T004_h4)

question: What type of cells make up the inner part of the adrenal gland (adrenal medulla), and where do they come from?

options.A: C cells derived from the embryonic pharyngeal pouches
options.B: Chromaffin cells, which are modified postganglionic sympathetic neurons
options.C: Epithelial cells arranged in hollow spherical follicles containing colloid
options.D: Follicular cells that synthesize and store mineralocorticoids

explanation: The adrenal medulla is unique! Its chromaffin cells are basically modified nerve cells that release adrenaline straight into your blood during a fight-or-flight moment.

question: Why do doctors prescribe a combination of different HIV drugs instead of just one?

options.A: To eliminate the need for routine laboratory viral load testing
options.B: To ensure the patient has fewer daily pills to swallow
options.C: To completely cure the patient of the infection within weeks
options.D: To prevent the virus from quickly mutating and developing drug resistance

explanation: Exactly! Hitting the virus from multiple angles makes it super hard for it to mutate and find a way around the medication.

question: How does poorly controlled diabetes mellitus make a patient more likely to catch infections?

options.A: High blood sugar levels create a favorable environment for pathogen growth and impair white blood cell function
options.B: It permanently destroys the skin, removing the body's primary mechanical barrier to the outside world
options.C: It causes immediate and total depletion of the body's red blood cell count
options.D: It forces the liver to produce antibodies that mistakenly attack healthy internal organs

explanation: Spot on! High sugar acts like food for germs, while making it harder for white blood cells to do their job of fighting back. Keep up the great work!

question: How is a painful muscle abscess caused by an unsterile injection usually managed?

options.A: Apply tight bandages to squeeze the trapped fluid out through the skin
options.B: Massage the lump firmly to help disperse the pus into surrounding tissue
options.C: Assist with surgical incision and drainage while maintaining sterile dressings
options.D: Advise the patient to ignore the lump until it dissolves on its own

explanation: Trapped pus has to come out! An abscess requires sterile incision and drainage, followed by proper wound care and antibiotics to help the patient heal.

question: A patient has patchy hair loss and scalp tenderness from wearing tight braids for months. What is the likely cause?

options.A: Pediculosis capitis
options.B: Alopecia areata
options.C: Traction alopecia
options.D: Seborrheic dermatitis

explanation: Constant pulling on the hair roots from tight hairstyles damages them over time, leading to hair loss known as traction alopecia. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T5#GNS112_U5_T5_h2)

question: What happens when someone consistently eats fewer calories than they burn?

options.A: The basal metabolic rate increases to compensate for lack of food
options.B: The digestive system shuts down completely to conserve water
options.C: The body breaks down stored fat and tissue to make up the deficit
options.D: The liver immediately converts the calorie shortage into new bone

explanation: If there's a calorie gap, the body gets resourceful—it dips into stored fat and muscle to find the energy it needs.

question: When does the diaphragm start moving back down to its usual position after birth?

options.A: Only when the mother starts breastfeeding
options.B: Six weeks after the baby is born
options.C: Immediately after the delivery of the placenta
options.D: Three months before labour begins

explanation: Once the baby and placenta are out, tummy crowding is instantly relieved and the diaphragm drops back down. Fantastic!

question: A patient has osteoarthritis in their knee. Which symptom are they most likely to feel?

options.A: Uncontrolled muscle twitching during periods of rest
options.B: Complete paralysis of the lower leg muscles
options.C: Rapid lengthening of the affected limb over weeks
options.D: Pain and stiffness that worsens with physical activity

explanation: Because osteoarthritis is wear-and-tear, moving the joint puts stress on the damaged cartilage and increases pain.

question: What is a core professional duty of a nurse caring for a PAC patient?

options.A: Providing unbiased, confidential, and compassionate medical care
options.B: Reporting the patient to local law enforcement authorities
options.C: Sharing clinical details publicly to educate the community
options.D: Refusing treatment if personal beliefs conflict with the diagnosis

explanation: You nailed it! As nurses, we are ethically bound to treat every patient with dignity, total confidentiality, and professional kindness.

question: How does MBO change performance evaluations for nurses?

options.A: Annual reviews are completely eliminated from the hospital
options.B: Manager opinions matter more than actual patient outcomes
options.C: Appraisals are judged against pre-agreed goals instead of subjective opinions
options.D: Evaluations are done in secret without the nurse knowing

explanation: MBO makes performance reviews objective because both parties measure success against clear targets they agreed on earlier. [learn more](GST321_U2_T4#GST321_U2_T4_h5)

question: What is the primary goal of nursing interventions in family-centered care?

options.A: To make all healthcare decisions on behalf of the household head
options.B: To strengthen the family's ability to care for its members independently
options.C: To permanently remove sick family members into institutions
options.D: To eliminate the need for doctors

explanation: Good nursing support empowers families so they gain confidence to manage their health challenges over time.

question: Why does the body slow down digestion during pregnancy?

options.A: To allow more time for absorbing nutrients
options.B: To keep the maternal body temperature stable
options.C: To reduce pressure on the urinary bladder
options.D: To prevent the stomach from overstretching

explanation: Think of it as a helpful feature: slower digestion gives the body extra time to soak up all those important vitamins and nutrients for the growing baby!

question: Why do doctors order an MRI when they suspect a neurodegenerative disease?

options.A: To directly count the number of living neurons
options.B: To cure abnormal protein accumulation
options.C: To visualize brain structures and rule out other causes
options.D: To measure electrical brain waves

explanation: An MRI gives a clear picture of the brain so doctors can check for things like strokes or tumors that might look like a degenerative disease. Smart nursing insight!
